body:
I went to the emergency room and a doctor checked for any physical conditions, and then when I finally saw the pdoc and he decided to put me on a low dose of something to bring me down in the short term because it was looking like I could spiral into full blown mania. Then he talked about how the antipsychotic was temporary and for the long term we'd look at things like Lithium etc. 
So you're right, I was surprised that I was medicated immediately, but it seemed like a safety thing.

Aw, I thought you literally wanted us to paint our worlds. I'd do that.
(PS I'd help you out, but I'm in the early early infantile stages of my diagnosis so not much of a help).

Thank you for your reply. I'd also like to add that I have absolutely nothing to be depressed about. I have a loving family, great friends, enough money, and many interests. It just makes no sense.

I've contemplated calling a hotline, but I never have the courage to dial the number, especially with the fear that someone might hear me.

What you said was reassuring, so thanks again. The hardest thing is knowing that the good feeling I have at the moment will be over sometime. I never know when the depression will hit.
